reviewed_relations: Exactly seven distinct inherited authority FDs are retained; user namespace comes from kernel NS_GET_USERNS on the held mount namespace rather than another caller-supplied FD or host PID scan
Actual initial user namespace inode and NS_GET_ID, direct userns parent and creator UID0 are checked; all six namespaces must be owned by the exact expected Main user namespace
Held root procfs/PID1 resolves actual init namespace links/root/start ticks and unchanged UID/GID map bodies before entry; maps must describe one non-host extent beginning at guest zero
Original supplementary groups are cleared before entering the user namespace; setresgid and setresuid explicitly select guest zero and all IDs/groups are checked
PDEATHSIG is rearmed after userns/gid/uid credential transitions and checked against the original held parent pidfd, retaining the post-transition failure boundary

PID setns affects the subsequent child; child arms parent death then polls the real entry-parent pidfd, checks original proc1 start epoch and executes; original entry parent waits and reaps the exact child
All inherited and kernel-derived authority descriptors have CLOEXEC before final exec; normal and failure paths close them through process retirement or File ownership
scope: Finite static tail review of actual FD derivation, credential transition and parent/Main lifetime checks
scope_limits: This helper does not authenticate or issue a Main witness. Caller must retain original daemon peer/socket/lease and full same-epoch Main authority throughout its bounded command and retirement.
Its root Node comparison is device/inode identity; it does not independently certify a mount graph or idmapped persistent data. Those remain caller/provider proof obligations.
The actual isolated R3 fixture/compilation reports are owned by the implementing agent; this review did not rerun them or claim Android production acceptance.
